title: Enterprise intake: standardize dedicated capacity SLAs, throughput tiers, and scaling guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Collect and prioritize incoming enterprise asks about Dedicated capacity commitments so we can propose a standardized set of SLA targets, reserved throughput tiers, GPU-class mappings, and scaling guardrails (bursting, preemption, and queueing) that are contract-ready. Context: Over the past quarter sales and solutions engineering have fielded 12 separate requests from enterprise prospects asking for different permutations of: predictable P95 latency targets, committed throughput (tokens/sec or rps), preferred GPU classes (A100 vs H100 vs LLM-optimized), and burst scaling behavior during traffic spikes. Without standardized tiers we are responding ad-hoc, slowing sales and creating engineering ambiguity. Goal: Produce a triaged intake report + recommended tier matrix and a short PRD for engineering implementation and legal contract language to enable consistent responses and faster closed-won cycles.
updates: 2026-02-12 - Aisha: Created ticket after weekly RTM with sales; compiled initial list of 7 enterprise asks into spreadsheet (link below).

2026-02-13 - Tom: Kickoff with SRE and Serving Eng. Captured technical constraints around guaranteed throughput vs. shared pools; noted 3 core blockers: preemption semantics, KV cache warmup, and cross-tenant isolation. Action: ENG to estimate work to surface capacity reservations in control plane (ENG-2143).

2026-02-15 - Tom: Hosted 60-min intake with Solutions/Legal/Product. Legal asked for initial SLA metrics: uptime (monthly), P95 latency, token completion success rate. Agreed to propose two tiers: Reserved and Reserved+Burst.

2026-02-17 - Priya (Solutions): Shared two customer readiness decks highlighting demand patterns (steady throughput vs. bursty inference). Noted one customer requires H100 for quantized LLMs due to long-context workloads. Added to GPU-class mapping discussion.

2026-02-18 - Eng (Emily): Quick feasibility: Reserved throughput enforced by token-budget throttles is feasible in 3 sprints; guaranteed P95 latency for long-tail inputs requires kernel scheduling improvements (ENG-3056).
2026-02-19 - Tom: Drafted a tier matrix and posted to #pm-dedicated-intake for feedback. Sales asked for one-off 'enterprise plus' option with SLA credits; Legal suggested standard credit table.
2026-02-20 - Aisha: Consolidated feedback and set next milestone: finalize tier definitions and acceptance criteria for engineering by 2026-02-27.
acceptance_criteria: A tier matrix (Reserved / Reserved+Burst / Enterprise Plus) with clear definitions for reserved throughput, burst allowances, and GPU-class options is approved by Eng, SRE, Sales, and Legal.
PRD describing control-plane changes to support capacity reservations, enforcement policy, and observability hooks (billing/metrics/tracing) is published.
Engineering provides an estimate and high-level rollout plan (canary + rollback) with a proposed release milestone and dependencies.
Standard SLA language (uptime, P95 latency, remediation credits) drafted and reviewed by Legal.
Customer-facing intake template and response time SLA for incoming asks (72 hours) established for Solutions/Sales team.
decisions: Adopt a three-tier model: Reserved (committed baseline with soft bursts), Reserved+Burst (predictable baseline + controlled burst window), Enterprise Plus (fully negotiated including dedicated GPU class and stronger SLAs).
Measure reserved throughput in qps or tokens/sec depending on product route; Sales to select metric per customer during intake.
Burst policy will be implemented as a time-windowed additive allowance (e.g., 3x baseline for 5 minutes) with guardrails to protect shared pools.
GPU class mapping: default to 'balanced' set (A100-80G equiv) for Reserved; Enterprise Plus may request H100 or other specialized hardware subject to availability and price uplift.
SLA credits table: use percentage-of-monthly-fee scheme (Legal to finalize).

Legal to draft initial SLA language and credits table (Priya + Legal, due 2026-02-25).
Solutions to pilot intake template with two current prospects and report back (Priya, due 2026-02-28).
Schedule 30-min cross-functional review on 2026-02-27 to approve matrix and PRD scope.
